note: Thomas (MFJ). Sole issue: American Opportunity Credit (sec. 25A(i)) for daughter ET in 2015. AOTC elected for ET in 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 (four prior taxable years), so sec. 25A(b)(2)(A) as modified by sec. 25A(i)(2) bars a 5th year: no AOTC for ET. Respondent conceded the AOTC for EMT and 2,885 of education expenses. As filed: nonrefundable education credit 3,000 and refundable AOTC 2,000. No income, deduction or tax figures in the opinion; sec. 25A not modelled; deficiency (5,000 per notice, before concessions) left to Rule 155. Only filing status encoded.

Kleinman. Filing status and dependent are not stated; two $4,000 exemptions (8,000) and itemized 9,250 (= 2015 HOH standard deduction) were claimed. HOH with one under-17 child (CTC) reproduces the notice's $10,518 exactly: corrected TI 83,712-9,250-8,000=66,462, 2015 HOH Tax Table 10,941 + sec. 223(f)(4) 20% tax 127 - CTC 550 (AGI phase-out 9x50) = 10,518; as filed TI 7,116 table tax 713 offset by nonrefundable CTC -> 0. Corrected wages = 24,366 reported + 58,712 A-1 (return omitted A-1 wages). HSA distribution 634 as otherIncome; sec. 223(f)(4)(A) tax 127 as otherTaxes. taxShown 0 (derived, not stated: no ACTC/EIC assumed claimed). Accuracy penalty conceded (not encoded); sec. 6673 penalty not imposed.

Arseo. Wages 25,687 (W-2 box 1; 2,890 pretax Arizona State Retirement System contribution excluded). Corrected: interest 25 and W-2G gambling winnings 2,994 included (otherIncome); gambling losses unsubstantiated (no records) and, even if allowed, as an itemized deduction (2,994) they would not exceed the 9,250 standard deduction; 6,500 IRA deduction denied (pretax contribution not deductible, §219). Filing status not stated: the 9,250 standard deduction shown is the 2015 head-of-household amount (single 6,300, MFJ 12,600), so hoh is encoded with no qualifying person/dependents, because the opinion finds none. Exemptions, dependents, EIC/CTC on the return are not in the opinion, so the 1,907 deficiency cannot be reproduced (see result notes). Gambling losses encoded as 0 (unsubstantiated). The 1,907 deficiency is not an expectation here: with the facts the opinion gives (hoh, one exemption, no EIC/CTC) the arithmetic gives about 1,067, so the return must have held facts (exemptions, credits) the opinion omits.
